suite.asserts_invariants_note: crates/fdd_rules/src/oracle_parity_test.rs is a real cross-implementation oracle harness (oracle_harness.rs) that asserts shipped SQL fault_hours against a pandas-equivalent confirm_fault reference on synthetic fixtures — genuine parity-testing infrastructure, not a rubber-stamp. claims_vs_code.claim: README: '62 fault-detection rules... published in two parity-matched flavors... the same rules' (SQL + Pandas)
claims_vs_code.evidence: sql_rules/registry.yaml has 68 rule_id entries (not 66 as README states, see C6). Of those, cookbook_catalog.py's RULES list has exactly 62 CookbookRule ids, and the two id-sets overlap almost completely by name (68 SQL ids minus 6 non-fault utility ids [AVG-ZONE-TEMP, FAN-RUNTIME-HOURS, FAULT-ELAPSED-HOURS, UTIL-INTERVAL, UTIL-MONTHLY, ZONE-COMFORT-PCT] = 62, matching the pandas catalog's 62 by name). So at the catalog level the '62 rules, same ids' claim holds. BUT for two of those matched-by-name rule pairs I read fully, the actual logic differs: (1) FC3 (sql_rules/fc3_mat_high.sql line 11: hardcoded epsilon literal 1.15 on all three temperature comparisons, no {{MIX_TOL}} placeholder, and registry.yaml's FC3 entry at line 376-388 has no `parameters:` block at all -- not tunable) vs open_fdd/rules/cookbook_catalog.py fc3() (line 623-635: reads eps_mat/eps_rat/eps_oat independently from the params dict, each defaulting to MIX_TOL=1.15 at line 536, but overridable) -- an operator-set tolerance override reaches pandas FC3 but is silently ignored by SQL FC3. (2) FC3 fan-on proof: SQL (fc3_mat_high.sql lines 9-13) prioritizes fan_status (threshold >0.05) over fan_cmd (threshold >0.01), defaulting fan_on=1 if both missing; pandas _fan() (cookbook_catalog.py lines 582-587) prioritizes fan-cmd over fan-status, and treats fan-status via as_bool() (no 0.05 threshold) -- when both signals are present and disagree, the two flavors read different reference. (3) VAV-2 (sql_rules/vav2_night_setback.sql lines 11-12) treats occ_mode as unoccupied only via an exact string match list including '0'/'0.0'; pandas _unoccupied_mask() (cookbook_catalog.py lines 927-938, also inlined at 1278-1283) additionally treats ANY numeric occ_mode <= 0.05 as unoccupied. A fractional occupancy signal like 0.03 is 'occupied' (no fault possible) under SQL VAV-2 but 'unoccupied' (fault-eligible) under pandas vav2() -- the two flavors disagree on whether a real data point is even eligible for this fault, before any threshold math runs. None of these three divergence sites are among the ~22 rule pairs covered by crates/fdd_rules/src/oracle_parity_test.rs, i.e. the project's own automated cross-check would not catch them.

claims_vs_code.claim: documented OPENFDD_JWT_SECRET='change-me' / OPENFDD_ADMIN_PASSWORD='change-me' run — is the placeholder silently accepted, and is there a hardcoded fallback secret when unset? (C3)
claims_vs_code.verdict: holds (no hidden fallback; placeholder is structurally rejected off-loopback)
claims_vs_code.evidence: services/central/src/auth.rs: is_loopback_bind() (lines 100-105) + assert_bind_auth_policy() (lines 108-150). Non-loopback bind fails closed with an explicit error if OPENFDD_JWT_SECRET is unset/empty (lines 126-132), or if it is set but under 32 characters (lines 133-138, 'change-me' is 9 chars so this would reject it automatically on any non-loopback bind), or if OPENFDD_ADMIN_PASSWORD is unset (lines 139-148). AuthConfig::load() (lines 152-186) never substitutes a default/hardcoded secret when the env var is unset -- `secret` stays None, `required()` returns false, and central logs 'auth_enabled=false ... open mode is loopback-only' (line 164). An explicit escape hatch OPENFDD_ALLOW_OPEN_BIND=1 (lines 116-125) bypasses this for CI/smoke, with a warn! log ('not internet-ready'). No hardcoded fallback secret found anywhere in auth.rs.

claims_vs_code.claim: MCP sidecar token (OPENFDD_MCP_TOKEN) scope: does it confer full admin? Can any tool mutate rules/config or reach the shell? (C4)
claims_vs_code.verdict: design_note (full-admin scope is documented/intentional; write tools are real but doubly gated; one advertised write tool has no live backing endpoint)
claims_vs_code.evidence: mcp/src/bridge.rs credentials_hint() (lines 10-39) documents the 'integrator' role as 'MCP JWT + dashboard admin -- preferred for OPENFDD_MCP_TOKEN' -- i.e. the MCP token is explicitly meant to be admin-equivalent, by design and by doc. mcp/src/protocol.rs tools_list() (~lines 60-200) exposes write tools that would mutate config/rules if live: openfdd_fdd_rules_save, openfdd_fdd_rules_activate, openfdd_fdd_run, openfdd_model_assignments_save, openfdd_csv_import_execute, openfdd_rules_batch, openfdd_reports_* writes. Every one of these is gated by mcp/src/gate.rs require_write_confirm() (lines 6-16): requires OPENFDD_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1 (an operator-set env flag, off by default) AND a per-call confirm:true. Checked the two scariest-sounding tools: openfdd_fdd_rules_save/openfdd_fdd_rules_activate reference POST /api/fdd-rules and POST /api/fdd-rules/{id}/activate -- grepping services/central/src/routes.rs's full route table (lines ~90-260) finds only `GET /api/fdd-rules` (line 125, fdd_rules_list) registered; no POST/activate handler exists in the routes I read, so these two MCP tools appear to reference an endpoint that does not exist server-side (would 404, not a live mutation path -- flag as documentation/tool-table drift, not a live escalation). openfdd_fdd_run *is* live (routes.rs line 115, POST /api/fdd/run) and its handler (line 1028) explicitly rejects any request carrying a raw `sql` field: 'raw SQL rejected on /api/fdd/run; use mode=registry with typed params' -- a real server-side safeguard against MCP-driven arbitrary SQL execution. Did not trace whether fdd_run enforces a JWT role check via router-level middleware (the handler signature itself takes no User/role extractor); not confirmed either way given time budget -- noted as a gap in my read, not a finding.

claims_vs_code.claim: MQTTS ingest -- can an unauthenticated client publish points; does central validate point identity? (C5)
claims_vs_code.verdict: holds (exceeds the LAN-scoping baseline: mTLS is enforced, not just network placement)
claims_vs_code.evidence: services/mqtt/mosquitto.conf: `allow_anonymous false`, `require_certificate true`, `use_identity_as_username true`, cafile/certfile/keyfile all set, `acl_file` configured -- an unauthenticated (uncertified) client cannot connect at all, let alone publish. crates/openfdd_mqtt/src/provision.rs provision_edge_kit() (lines 34-157) issues a per-edge client certificate and writes a per-edge mosquitto ACL scoping that edge's user (`edge:<site_id>:<edge_id>`) to only its own topic-write patterns (lines 129-144, via TopicBuilder::edge_acl_patterns()). I did not verify the topic pattern granularity is fine enough to prevent one legitimately-provisioned edge from publishing under a *different* equipment_id within the same site/edge namespace (would need to read openfdd_contracts::TopicBuilder in full) -- flagged as a residual open question, not a confirmed gap.

claims_vs_code.claim: update script 'pull, backup, rollback if health fails' -- does rollback actually restore, or can a failed update lose the historian? (C8)
claims_vs_code.verdict: latent (mechanism exists and correctly restores container images, but the 'backup' does not cover data)
claims_vs_code.evidence: scripts/openfdd_maint_update_resume.sh snapshot() (lines ~108-142) saves: a redacted copy of .env, `docker ps` output, and old image digests to $SNAP_DIR/state.json. It does NOT snapshot the Arrow/Feather historian, the SQL rule registry, or any application database. rollback() (lines ~144-186) restores the OLD container image digests via OPENFDD_*_IMAGE env vars and re-runs openfdd_stack_up.sh --no-pull -- this correctly undoes a bad *code* deploy. But if the new version's startup/migration path had already mutated on-disk historian data before the health check (openfdd_stack_wait_health, scripts/openfdd_stack_up.sh line 110) failed, that data mutation is not backed up and rollback cannot undo it -- the script only ever reverts which container image runs, never what the containers wrote to the mounted volumes. I found no evidence in the scripts I read of an active migration step that mutates the historian in place (scripts/openfdd_stack_up.sh has no migration/historian-touching code in the ~122 lines I read), so this is a latent gap in the backup design rather than a demonstrated data-loss bug today.

most_damning_claim: README's '62 fault-detection rules published in two parity-matched flavors ... the same rules' is contradicted by FC3's tolerance parameter being tunable in the pandas flavor (open_fdd/rules/cookbook_catalog.py:623-635, eps_mat/eps_rat/eps_oat from params) but hardcoded and non-tunable in the SQL flavor (sql_rules/fc3_mat_high.sql:25-26, literal 1.15, no registry parameters block for FC3) -- an operator adjusting the tolerance dashboard-side changes what the pandas cookbook flags without changing what the production SQL registry flags for the identical rule id.

security_escalation.note: No live, unauthenticated-exploitable escalation found. Auth fails closed off-loopback with no hardcoded fallback secret (services/central/src/auth.rs). MQTT ingest requires mTLS client certs, allow_anonymous false (services/mqtt/mosquitto.conf). MCP write tools require an operator-set env flag plus per-call confirm, and the one live rule-execution endpoint explicitly rejects raw SQL (services/central/src/routes.rs:1028-1032). Two MCP tool entries (fdd_rules_save/activate) advertise write capability against an endpoint that does not appear to exist server-side -- a documentation/dead-code gap, not an exploit. Update rollback does not cover data (scripts/openfdd_maint_update_resume.sh) -- a latent operational-safety gap, not a security escalation.

tier_m.why: Two genuine, citable, non-security correctness findings (FC3 tunability/fan-priority drift, VAV-2 occupancy-threshold drift) directly falsify the flagship 'the same rules' parity claim in a small but real way, both landing outside the project's own oracle-parity test coverage -- exactly the failure mode the pre-registration predicted. No security escalation was found; auth, MQTT ingest, and MCP write-gating all held up better than the LAN-scoping baseline required. The read covered the claim-bearing surfaces named in the plan (rule catalogs, auth, MCP, MQTT, update script) but not the full 144k-LOC repo (React frontend internals, most of central's routes.rs, the edge/OT buildroot image were not read) -- HOLD reflects real findings worth a maintainer's attention plus an intentionally partial read, not a security-flag-forced hold.

prediction_graded: CORRECT. Plan predicted 1-2 correctness findings from C1 parity drift and C2 NaN/missing handling, and 0 security escalations. Found exactly that shape: 2 correctness findings (FC3 drift counted as one rule-pair finding with two facets; VAV-2 drift), both landing in the C1/C2 space the plan named, and 0 security escalations across C3/C4/C5/C8. The plan's framing that 'if the rule sets are truly parity-matched, that is a notable clean result' also partially applies: the catalog-level id-count match (62=62) is clean, and the ~22 oracle-tested pairs showed no divergence in my reading -- the drift is real but narrower than a wholesale parity failure.
one_line: The 62-rule SQL/Pandas catalogs match by id and mostly by test coverage, but at least two rule pairs (FC3, VAV-2) genuinely diverge in threshold tunability and NaN/occupancy-boundary handling, outside the project's own oracle-parity test net; no security escalation found, and MQTT/auth/MCP write-gating all held up.

Fan-signal priority divergence confirmed: SQL :10-13 prefers fan_status (>0.05) then fan_cmd (>0.01), default ON; pandas _fan() prefers fan-cmd then fan-status via as_bool(), default 1.0. '0','0.0'); pandas _unoccupied_mask (cookbook_catalog.py:927-938) adds numeric occ_num <= 0.05 — a numeric 0.03 is unoccupied in pandas, occupied in SQL.
